spatial_claims.claim: Diagonals from A_1 to A_3,...,A_{n-1} divide the convex polygon into a fan of n-2 triangles T_i = triangle(A_1, A_i, A_{i+1}), all diagonals lying inside the polygon
At vertex A_2, the polygon angle equals the included angle of triangle T_2, with containing sides A_1A_2 and A_2A_3

At each interior vertex A_i (i=3,...,n-1), the polygon angle decomposes additively: angle(A_{i-1},A_i,A_{i+1}) = angle(A_{i-1},A_i,A_1) + angle(A_1,A_i,A_{i+1}), requiring ray A_iA_1 between rays A_iA_{i-1} and A_iA_{i+1}
Adjacent fan triangles T_i and T_{i+1} share the diagonal A_1A_{i+1}, and corresponding pair U_i, U_{i+1} share B_1B_{i+1}
Both t_i:u_i and t_{i+1}:u_{i+1} equal the duplicate ratio of A_1A_{i+1}:B_1B_{i+1} via 6.19, using the shared diagonal as corresponding side in both pairs of similar triangles

configuration_map: Vertex A_1 is a designated vertex of the convex polygon A_1A_2...A_n. Diagonals A_1A_3, A_1A_4, ..., A_1A_{n-1} all lie inside the polygon, creating a fan of n-2 triangles. At each intermediate vertex A_i (i=3,...,n-1), the diagonal A_1A_i partitions the polygon angle into two sub-angles, one belonging to triangle T_{i-1} and the other to T_i. Ray A_iA_1 lies interior to the polygon angle at A_i, falling between rays A_iA_{i-1} and A_iA_{i+1}. The same fan structure applies to the second polygon B_1B_2...B_n with corresponding diagonals from B_1. All constructed points and lines remain within their respective polygons throughout the proof.
pass_reason: All spatial claims are mutually consistent. The fan triangulation from vertex A_1 of a convex polygon produces diagonals that lie inside the polygon, validating the angle decompositions at each interior vertex. The shared-diagonal structure between adjacent fan triangles is a direct consequence of the construction. The bulk of the proof is proportional and algebraic reasoning (Book 5 and 6 results) with no geometric configuration issues.
